steps.text: Set the risk parameters, decide between automatic and manual, and practise on the demo account.

pros: Fast setup - minutes to a live dashboard.
cons: Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
redFlags: A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.
Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.

faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$200, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$200 minimum.

bottomLine: Solva Formheim does what it says mechanically - signals, two modes, a broker partner. The open questions are pricing clarity and verification, both solvable by reading before funding.
The final score lands at 4.6 - a capable platform held back by its own paperwork. Start small, verify the claims yourself and never trade money you cannot lose.
